title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls with robust injection and retry semantics
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Customer workloads and internal canaries surfaced recurring issues when a single user request invoked multiple tools in parallel: incorrect ordering of tool-result injection, inconsistent retry behavior across tool failures, and poor streaming stability for partial tool outputs. Motivation: Make the tool-calling execution model deterministic and ergonomic for app developers while keeping the runtime performant. Goals: (1) support ordered and parallel tool invocations with consistent injection semantics, (2) implement idempotent retry paths for transient failures, (3) preserve streaming of tool outputs and partial model responses, and (4) be backward compatible with existing OpenAI-compat calls unless explicit flags are enabled. Implementation: Introduce a ToolExecutionPlan that flattens multi-tool/parallel invocations into an ordered execution graph at request start. Each tool call is annotated with: id, dependencies (for ordered injection), retry policy (none/linear/exponential), and injection_strategy (append/replace/merge). The runtime scheduler executes independent tools in parallel up to a configurable concurrency cap and applies the requested injection strategy deterministically based on dependency resolution. Retries are executed with idempotency keys and a max_attempts guard; transient failures surface structured error objects to the model as tool_result with metadata (attempts, last_error). Streaming: tool stdout/stderr and partial results are forwarded as streaming events and injected into the model stream using a stable marker protocol to avoid interleaving with model tokens. OpenAI-compat: This change keeps the current behaviour as default but introduces the new execution flags in the API and SDKs: tool_execution_plan and tool_retry_policy. Backwards compatibility is preserved unless an API consumer opts into the new flags. Tests & rollout: added unit tests for graph resolution, e2e tests with mock tool servers to validate parallel runs and retries, and a perf canary on canary/redwood-tool-exec cluster. Feature gated behind runtime.flag.tool_execution_v2; gradual rollout to 10% of traffic after merge, then 100% after monitoring for 48h. See the checklist below for details and the conversation history for reviewer suggestions.

review_comments: Ethan Zhang: Nice design. Two asks: add microbenchmarks for parallel executor and ensure the concurrency cap is configurable per-tenant.
Ava Martinez: Added a perf canary and per-tenant cap (runtime.config.max_tool_concurrency). See parallel_executor.go changes.
Priya Nair: The retry semantics look sensible but we should avoid re-injecting partial results after a successful retry — prefer replacing on success to avoid model confusion.
Ava Martinez: Implemented injection_strategy with 'replace' as the default for retries. Updated docs and tests.
Luca Rossi: Found a race where the injection buffer could emit interleaved streaming markers under high concurrency. Requesting buffer locking or an ordered emitter.
Ava Martinez: Fixed with ordered emission queue and added test that reproduces high-concurrency interleaving. Marking as resolved.
Ethan Zhang: Approving after the perf numbers and a small nits pass on SDK examples.
Priya Nair: Approved. Recommend a gradual rollout and alert on tool_result_error_rate > 1%.

rollout_plan: Enable runtime.flag.tool_execution_v2 in canary cluster and run perf canary for 24h
Roll out to 10% of traffic on hosted API for 48h while monitoring tool_result_error_rate and stream_interleaving alerts
If no regressions, increase to 100% over 12h and monitor for 48h
If a regression is detected, toggle runtime.flag.tool_execution_v2=false to fall back to legacy execution model
release_notes: Introduce Tool Execution v2 behind feature flag: deterministic injection ordering, configurable per-tool retry policies, and parallel execution with concurrency caps.
Streaming stability improvements: stable markers prevent interleaving of partial tool output with model tokens.
SDKs: new helper APIs to construct tool_execution_plan and specify retry_policy.
Backward compatible by default; opt-in via runtime.flag.tool_execution_v2 or API flags.
notes: Follow-up work: integrate with routing policies to prefer cheaper model variants when tools are slow (ENG-2201).
Consider adding a diagnostic header to responses that indicates which tools retried and how many attempts were made.
Docs: add a migration guide for customers who relied on implicit injection ordering.
